rsa_ladder.label: 15 = 3 x 5
rsa_ladder.method: Shor's algorithm on 7-qubit NMR quantum computer

rsa_ladder.label: 21 = 3 x 7
rsa_ladder.method: Shor's algorithm on photonic quantum computer
rsa_ladder.note: Largest number factored by Shor's on quantum hardware

rsa_ladder.label: ~100-bit semiprime
rsa_ladder.signal: Proves the physics works at meaningful scale without classical shortcuts

rsa_ladder.label: RSA-512
rsa_ladder.signal: THE CANARY. Hockey stick begins. Breaking RSA becomes an engineering problem.

rsa_ladder.label: RSA-1024
rsa_ladder.signal: Legacy systems fall. Mass migration urgency.

ecdlp_ladder.label: 6-bit ECDLP
ecdlp_ladder.method: Shor's variant on public quantum cloud hardware
ecdlp_ladder.note: Largest public quantum ECDLP attack on record (the April 2026 15-bit claim was refuted)

ecdlp_ladder.label: 15-bit ECDLP (Bitcoin-style key)
ecdlp_ladder.method: Shor's variant on ~70-qubit public cloud quantum device
ecdlp_ladder.source: Giancarlo Lelli, Project Eleven Q-Day Prize (1 BTC bounty, April 2026)
ecdlp_ladder.note: Awarded 1 BTC by Project Eleven, but the quantum contribution is refuted: replacing the IBM device output with random bits (/dev/urandom) still recovers the key, and the author's README calls the output 'indistinguishable from uniform random sampling.' Not counted as a quantum ECDLP record.

ecdlp_ladder.label: 64-bit ECDLP
ecdlp_ladder.signal: Proof of concept for quantum ECDLP

ecdlp_ladder.label: 128-bit ECDLP
ecdlp_ladder.signal: THE CANARY. Engineering sprint begins. Blockchain migration race starts.

ecdlp_ladder.label: 256-bit ECDLP (secp256k1)
ecdlp_ladder.signal: Q-DAY (Blockchain). Bitcoin and Ethereum keys breakable.

classical_context.label: RSA-250 (829 bits)
classical_context.note: Largest RSA number factored by any method

ai_cryptanalysis.label: 112-bit prime-field ECDLP (secp112r1)
ai_cryptanalysis.method: Classical parallel Pollard rho on ~200 PlayStation 3 consoles
ai_cryptanalysis.source: Bos, Kaihara, Kleinjung, Lenstra, Montgomery — Solving a 112-bit prime elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem on game consoles
ai_cryptanalysis.note: Largest public classical prime-field ECDLP solve. secp256k1 is 256-bit; generic attacks need ~2^128 work.

ai_cryptanalysis.label: HAWK-256 key recovery (NIST additional-signature candidate)
ai_cryptanalysis.method: AI-discovered lattice automorphism (Anthropic Claude Mythos Preview); key recovery cost ~2^64 to ~2^38; ~60 hours, ~$100K compute
ai_cryptanalysis.note: First verified AI-found break of a standardization-track scheme. HAWK team confirmed and withdrew from NIST. Young (~4-year) assumption, smallest parameter set; nothing deployed affected.

ai_cryptanalysis.label: AI refutes fine-grained complexity conjectures (integer multiplication, 3SUM, APSP)
ai_cryptanalysis.method: OpenAI 722-manuscript release: multiplication in O(n (log n)^(1-k)), k = 2^-182; separately reported 3SUM in n^1.9992
ai_cryptanalysis.note: Not cryptanalysis — asymptotic improvements with no practical effect. Cited by Justin Drake ('bunker mode', 2026-10-07) as evidence that AI-accelerated math could break ECDSA. No ECDLP or RSA result published.

ai_cryptanalysis.label: AI labs reportedly probing deployed cryptographic primitives
ai_cryptanalysis.method: Reported internal testing of frontier models against cryptographic protocols and primitives
ai_cryptanalysis.note: Scott Aaronson, citing anonymous sources (2026-10-07). An investigation, not a result: no lab, model, scheme, or outcome named.

ai_cryptanalysis.label: AI reconstructs NIST P-curve seed generation (no weakness found)
ai_cryptanalysis.method: Anthropic Claude identified lrand48 LCG output in the 1997–98 NIST seeds; recovered the 48-bit state via LLL lattice reduction and reversed it to Unix-timestamp seeds
ai_cryptanalysis.note: Provenance, not a break — Anthropic: 'not a cryptographic break, new attack, or weakness'; raises confidence P-curves carry no backdoor. secp256k1 not involved (Koblitz curve, no seed). First published frontier-lab analysis of a deployed curve: capability datapoint, null security result.
